For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

content.text:
**Finding: missing (INSURANCE)** — validated redline submitted.

- **Investigation:** A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits. Section 10 (General Provisions, p0059–p0070) covers Notices, No Joint Venture, Assignment, Waiver, Governing Law, Severability, Survival, Entire Agreement and Headings/Counterparts — no coverage requirement anywhere, and no indemnity clause either.
- **Why it matters:** HDI develops and hosts the Site, and Section 8.1 confirms it has access to "Content, user information, data" of the Company. A hosting vendor processing Customer Data with zero insurance sits in the rule's walk-away zone, not the fallback.
- **Fix:** Inserted a new Section 10.9 (Insurance) after p0070 at the preferred limits — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, running through the term plus one year. The comment flags the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a negotiable landing spot if HDI's existing program can't reach the preferred limits.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and Section 10 (General Provisions, p0059–p0070) runs from Notices through Headings/Counterparts with no coverage requirement. HDI develops and hosts the Site and, per Section 8.1, has access to Content, user information and data of the Company, so it is a vendor processing Customer Data with no insurance obligation at all — walk-away territory under the rule. We inserted a new Section 10.9 at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) flagged in the comment as a discussion point.

Original paragraphs:
p0059: 10. General Provisions.
p0070: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0070: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.
10.9 Insurance. HDI shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. HDI shall provide the Company with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as the Agreement contains none and HDI hosts the Site and handles Company and customer data. Our position is commercial general liability of USD 1M/2M, errors and omissions of USD 2M and cyber liability of USD 5M, with certificates on request; we can discuss lower E&O and cyber limits if HDI's existing program requires it.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI — provider/host).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI — provider/host).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual corporate representations (organization, authority, enforceability, no conflicts) at p0056–p0057 and an HDI acknowledgement regarding the Globix Agreement at p0058. Nowhere in the Agreement (including HDI's Responsibilities in Sections 1.1–1.8 and the Site management provisions in Section 5) does HDI warrant that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, that the Site will conform to approved specifications or documentation for any period, or provide any repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy; there is also no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty running to us. That fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) because there is no conformance warranty or remedy at all. Mitigating factor: there is no "AS IS" disclaimer, so this is not walk-away territory, and Section 1.6 gives us a termination right if the Site is not operational on time. Redline inserts a new Section 9(c) at the preferred position (professional and workmanlike Services, 90-day conformance warranty for the Site, compliance with laws, no malicious code, with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy at HDI's option); a shorter conformance period is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Add an HDI performance/conformance warranty with repair, replace or refund remedy in Section 9.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains only mutual corporate authority representations, so HDI gives no warranty at all for the Site or the hosting Services; we added a standard performance and conformance warranty with a repair, replace, re-perform or refund remedy, plus compliance with laws and no malicious code. If helpful, we can accept a ninety (90) day conformance period for the Site as a fallback.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI — provider/host).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Nowhere in the Agreement (including HDI's Responsibilities in Sections 1.1–1.8 and the Site management provisions in Section 5) does HDI warrant that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, that the Site will conform to approved specifications or documentation for any period, or provide any repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy; there is also no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty running to us. That fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) because there is no conformance warranty or remedy at all. Mitigating factor: there is no "AS IS" disclaimer, so this is not walk-away territory, and Section 1.6 gives us a termination right if the Site is not operational on time. Redline inserts a new Section 9(c) at the preferred position (professional and workmanlike Services, 90-day conformance warranty for the Site, compliance with laws, no malicious code, with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy at HDI's option); a shorter conformance period is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Add an HDI performance/conformance warranty with repair, replace or refund remedy in Section 9.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains only mutual corporate authority representations, so HDI gives no warranty at all for the Site or the hosting Services; we added a standard performance and conformance warranty with a repair, replace, re-perform or refund remedy, plus compliance with laws and no malicious code. If helpful, we can accept a ninety (90) day conformance period for the Site as a fallback.

ops.text: (c) HDI represents and warrants to the Company that (1) the Services (including the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance, management and hosting of the Site) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (2) for a period of ninety (90) days following the Effective Date, the Site will conform in all material respects to the specifications and Content approved by the Company pursuant to Section 5.2 and to any documentation provided by HDI; (3) HDI will perform the Services in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations; and (4) the Site and any software provided by HDI will not contain any virus, worm, disabling code or other malicious code. The Company's remedy for breach of this warranty shall be, at HDI's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming portion of the Site, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services.

HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.
input.rationale: Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the operative access/use grant, but it runs to "the Company" alone: no affiliates, no contractors acting on our behalf, and no written-notice mechanic to add them. That fails a material term of the fallback, which requires at minimum affiliate coverage on written notice plus successor transferability. The gap is not merely one of silence: Section 10.3 (p0063) provides that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which affirmatively excludes our affiliates and contractors from exercising the Section 1.4 rights and leaves no path to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger. Section 10.3 is otherwise a standard binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause; it confirms the Agreement inures to successors but does not itself grant an affirmative right to transfer the licence in an M&A transaction, so it only weakly supports the second fallback element and cannot cure the missing affiliate and contractor coverage. The redline makes the smallest edits to reach the preferred position: it extends the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf and to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and carves those parties out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3. The comment offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback. The grant is not expressed to be revocable at HDI's discretion, so no revocability deletion is needed, and the term/termination mechanics are addressed under the term rule.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to the Company's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf and to a successor in an M&A transaction, and carve them out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (and to a successor in a merger or sale of the business), since our group and outsourced providers need to operate and monitor the Site; our playbook requires affiliate and contractor coverage plus successor transferability. We also carved those parties out of the "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" language in Section 10.3, which as drafted would exclude them; if you prefer, we can accept affiliates being added on written notice to HDI.

The access and use rights granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 may be exercised by the Company, its affiliates (meaning any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with the Company) and any contractors acting on the Company's behalf, and may be transferred to any successor to the Company's business by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.

- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI — provider/host).

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.
input.rationale: Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the operative grant in our favour: HDI must provide the Company with access to, and the right to use, the hosting system and HDI's software and Content administration tools. The grant carries none of the walk-away features — it is not stated to be revocable at HDI's discretion, is not labelled "non-transferable" or "solely for internal use", and contains no exclusion of affiliates or contractors, so there is no restriction preventing the Company from having its affiliates or contractors exercise the access on its behalf. Section 10.3 (Assignment) provides that the Agreement is binding upon and inures to the benefit of the parties' legal representatives, successors and assigns, which supplies the successor/M&A transfer element of the fallback. The clause therefore sits at the fallback rather than the preferred position: affiliates and contractors are not expressly named and there is no express notice mechanic to add them, and the access right runs only with the term of the Agreement rather than being perpetual/irrevocable (the term and 90-day termination mechanics are addressed under the term rule, not here). Those are sub-elements short of the preferred wording and, given the unrestricted bare access right in a hosting arrangement where the Company is the intended user, they do not warrant a redline.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

- **Grant clause:** §1.4 (p0008–p0009) is the operative licence/access grant running in our favour — HDI must give the Company access to, and the right to use, the hosting system plus HDI's software and Content administration tools.
- **No walk-away triggers:** the grant is not revocable at HDI's discretion, is not styled "non-exclusive, non-transferable," is not limited to "internal use," and contains no exclusion of affiliates or contractors — so there is no restriction to strike.
- **Successor transfer:** §10.3 (p0063) makes the Agreement binding on and enforceable by the parties' legal representatives, successors and assigns, satisfying the fallback's M&A/successor limb.
- **Noted, not flagged:** affiliates and contractors are not expressly named (no written-notice mechanic), and the access right is coextensive with the term rather than perpetual/irrevocable. These are sub-elements short of the preferred position; the term/termination mechanics belong to the term rule, so they are recorded in the rationale rather than redlined.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual corporate representations (organization, authority, enforceability, no conflicts) at p0056–p0057 and an HDI acknowledgement regarding the Globix Agreement at p0058. Nowhere in the Agreement (including HDI's Responsibilities in Sections 1.1–1.8 and the Site management provisions in Section 5) does HDI warrant that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, that the Site will conform to approved specifications or documentation for any period, or provide any repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy; there is also no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty running to us. That fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) because there is no conformance warranty or remedy at all. Mitigating factor: there is no "AS IS" disclaimer, so this is not walk-away territory, and Section 1.6 gives us a termination right if the Site is not operational on time. Redline inserts a new Section 9(c) at the preferred position (professional and workmanlike Services, 90-day conformance warranty for the Site, compliance with laws, no malicious code, with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy at HDI's option); a shorter conformance period is available as a fallback.

Original paragraphs:
p0055: 9. Warranties.
p0056: (a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,
p0057: power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity.
p0058: (b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date

p0058: (b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date
(c) HDI represents and warrants to the Company that (1) the Services (including the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance, management and hosting of the Site) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (2) for a period of ninety (90) days following the Effective Date, the Site will conform in all material respects to the specifications and Content approved by the Company pursuant to Section 5.2 and to any documentation provided by HDI; (3) HDI will perform the Services in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations; and (4) the Site and any software provided by HDI will not contain any virus, worm, disabling code or other malicious code. The Company's remedy for breach of this warranty shall be, at HDI's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming portion of the Site, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the operative access/use grant, but it runs to "the Company" alone: no affiliates, no contractors acting on our behalf, and no written-notice mechanic to add them. That fails a material term of the fallback, which requires at minimum affiliate coverage on written notice plus successor transferability. The gap is not merely one of silence: Section 10.3 (p0063) provides that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which affirmatively excludes our affiliates and contractors from exercising the Section 1.4 rights and leaves no path to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger. Section 10.3 is otherwise a standard binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause; it confirms the Agreement inures to successors but does not itself grant an affirmative right to transfer the licence in an M&A transaction, so it only weakly supports the second fallback element and cannot cure the missing affiliate and contractor coverage. The redline makes the smallest edits to reach the preferred position: it extends the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf and to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and carves those parties out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3. The comment offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback. The grant is not expressed to be revocable at HDI's discretion, so no revocability deletion is needed, and the term/termination mechanics are addressed under the term rule.

Original paragraphs:
p0008: 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and
p0009: the right to use, a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated, with a direct Internet connection of shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth, plus capacity to process continuously during burst periods. HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.
p0063: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
HDI: This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
Company: This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".

Rendered redline:
p0009: the right to use, a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated, with a direct Internet connection of shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth, plus capacity to process continuously during burst periods. HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information. The access and use rights granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 may be exercised by the Company, its affiliates (meaning any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with the Company) and any contractors acting on the Company's behalf, and may be transferred to any successor to the Company's business by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.
p0063: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but, other than the Company's affiliates and contractors acting on the Company's behalf (which may exercise the rights granted to the Company under Section 1.4), no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (and to a successor in a merger or sale of the business), since our group and outsourced providers need to operate and monitor the Site; our playbook requires affiliate and contractor coverage plus successor transferability. We also carved those parties out of the "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" language in Section 10.3, which as drafted would exclude them; if you prefer, we can accept affiliates being added on written notice to HDI.

input.quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
input.rationale:
The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall payment or volume cap on the Company. The sole compensation to HDI (§ 3.1) is a pure revenue share — 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold — so the Company pays only on actual sales achieved and owes nothing if the Site generates no revenue; the $11,000 figure is a floor below which no fee accrues, which benefits us rather than functioning as a minimum spend. There is no guaranteed hosting volume or committed order quantity anywhere in the document (searches for "minimum", "commit", "volume" return nothing on point). The term is a one-year term with annual auto-renewal terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (§ 4.1), so we also have a standing exit. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only).

Two adjacent terms noted but not deviations under this rule: (i) the Termination Payment in § 4.2 is an exit fee calculated as half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000 — it is triggered by, and scales with, actual sales rather than by any purchase shortfall, and it is expressly zero where the formula yields zero or less, so it is not a take-or-pay penalty (any concern with its size belongs to the termination-fee rule, not here); and (ii) the § 6.1 exclusivity restricts the Company from running a similar Deerskin Products site elsewhere, which is a channel/exclusivity restriction rather than a volume commitment and is properly addressed under the exclusivity rule.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice, the Termination Date and the Termination Payment; there is no exit, transition-assistance, data return/export or deletion language anywhere in the Agreement (searches for transition, migration, return, delete/destroy return nothing, and the confidentiality provisions in Section 8 contain no return-or-destroy obligation). In a hosting arrangement where HDI holds our Content, user information and customer data, the absence leaves us with no right to our data or migration help on exit — below the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). Proposed new Section 4.3 inserted after the Termination Payment mechanics gives six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, 30-day return in machine-readable format, and deletion with written certification.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months of transition assistance and to return and then certify deletion of Company Content and data on termination.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a wind-down provision because the Agreement is silent on exit: on termination HDI must give us up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our Content, user information and other data within thirty days in a machine-readable format, and then delete and certify deletion. We can accept a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including cooperation in migrating the Site and its operation to the Company or its designee, for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of the Company's request, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer files, transaction records and other data of the Company in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Content, user information and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. HDI shall not delete, withhold or render inaccessible any such Content, user information or data prior to completing its obligations under this Section 4.3.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI — provider/host).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement contains no take-or-pay exposure for us:

- **§ 3.1 — fees track actual results only.** HDI's sole compensation is 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per calendar month. We pay nothing if the Site generates no revenue, and the $11,000 threshold is a floor *below* which no fee accrues — it operates in our favour, not as a minimum spend. This satisfies the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only).
- **§ 4.1 — standing exit.** One-year term with annual auto-renewal, terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so even a commitment reading would have a clean exit.
- Targeted searches for "minimum", "commit" and "volume" returned nothing on point; there is no guaranteed hosting volume, committed order quantity or shortfall payment.

Two adjacent terms I reviewed and deliberately did **not** flag here:

1. **§ 4.2 Termination Payment** — an exit fee of half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000, expressly zero where the formula yields zero or less. It is triggered by and scales *with* actual sales rather than by any purchase shortfall, so it is not a take-or-pay penalty. Its magnitude is a termination-fee question, not a minimum-commitment one, and flagging it here would double-count the same commercial term.
2. **§ 6.1 Exclusivity** — bars us from a similar Deerskin Products site elsewhere during the term. That is a channel restriction rather than a volume cap on our usage, and belongs to the exclusivity rule.

Both are recorded in the rationale for the reviewing team rather than redlined under MINCOMMIT.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall payment or volume cap on the Company. There is no guaranteed hosting volume or committed order quantity anywhere in the document (searches for "minimum", "commit", "volume" return nothing on point). The term is a one-year term with annual auto-renewal terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (§ 4.1), so we also have a standing exit. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice, the Termination Date and the Termination Payment; there is no exit, transition-assistance, data return/export or deletion language anywhere in the Agreement (searches for transition, migration, return, delete/destroy return nothing, and the confidentiality provisions in Section 8 contain no return-or-destroy obligation). In a hosting arrangement where HDI holds our Content, user information and customer data, the absence leaves us with no right to our data or migration help on exit — below the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). Proposed new Section 4.3 inserted after the Termination Payment mechanics gives six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, 30-day return in machine-readable format, and deletion with written certification.

p0029: (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

We added a Section 5.5 reaching the preferred position: Company ownership of the Site, deliverables and customer data with an HDI assignment, HDI retention of its pre-existing software and tools, and a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any HDI materials embedded in the Site.","proposal":"Add a Section 5.5 ownership clause: Company owns the Site, deliverables and customer data; HDI retains background IP and grants a perpetual licence back; no joint ownership.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-e06a621a","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"A full sweep of the document (searches for "liability", "consequential", "in no event", "damages", "indemnif" and a read of the General Provisions, Warranties and Confidentiality sections) shows no limitation of liability, no aggregate cap and no exclusion of consequential damages anywhere. Basis: full reads of sec-p0001, sec-1.4, sec-5.4 (including the General Manager/liaison appointment at p0035, the point at which named individuals are put in contact and where a reciprocal no-hire would typically sit), Exclusivity §6, Confidentiality §8, Warranties §9 and General Provisions §10, plus targeted searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ", "employ or engage", "induce", "personnel" and "directly or indirectly". {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI / Company Internet Site Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — findings, redlines and walk-away exposure

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is a revenue-share hosting and site-development arrangement, and several of its terms are favourable to us: there is no MFN obligation, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment (fees accrue only on Net Sales above the $11,000 monthly floor), no non-solicitation covenant binding us, New York law governs (§ 10.5), and HDI carries a heavier two-year post-term restriction under § 6.3.

The problem is what the Agreement omits. There is **no indemnification of any kind**, **no intellectual property ownership provision**, **no limitation of liability or cap**, **no performance warranty**, **no transition-assistance or data-return obligation**, and **no insurance covenant** — this in an arrangement where HDI builds and hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer data. Three of those gaps (vendor IP indemnity, insurance for a vendor processing Customer Data, and the effective exclusion of our affiliates and contractors from the § 1.4 grant via § 10.3) sit in walk-away territory under the playbook.

Separately, the exit economics are materially off-market for us. Our convenience right in § 4.1 is real on its face but is priced by the § 4.2 Termination Payment — 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000, uncapped, payable by the Company alone and triggered by essentially any Company termination. Combined with the indefinite § 6.1 exclusivity (auto-renewing term, no performance-based release), our ability to leave a failing engagement is illusory. These are our principal negotiation asks alongside the missing ri[REDACTED] provisions.

One finding (non-solicitation) did not clear verification and is carried as **needs review** rather than as a conclusion; one finding (licence scope) was repaired on verification.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | New § 9(c) proposed (Warranties) | No indemnity, hold-harmless or defence language anywhere; § 9 is corporate reps plus the Globix carve-out only. Walk-away territory given HDI supplies software, technology and hosting. Preferred HDI indemnity inserted (third-party IP, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation mechanics, sited in § 9 so it survives under § 10.7. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | New § 5.5 proposed | No ownership or assignment clause; nothing states who owns the Site, the deliverables we fund, our Content or customer data, and there is no licence back of HDI platform IP. Mitigant: no assignment of Company IP or data to HDI and § 10.2 disclaims co-ownership. Proposed § 5.5 gives Company ownership plus HDI assignment, HDI retains background IP, perpetual royalty-free licence back. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | New § 10.9 proposed | No cap, no exclusion of consequential damages; the only "liability" references are in the no-joint-venture clause (§ 10.2). Both parties, including us, face unlimited exposure. Inserted mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1,000,000, mutual indirect-damages exclusion, uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmation that our § 3 / § 4.2 payment obligations are not capped damages. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (with § 4.1, § 4.2, § 1.6) | Category is defined, but the restriction runs for the whole term and § 4.1 auto-renews annually, so it is potentially indefinite; the only exit is terminating the Agreement, which can trigger the § 4.2 Termination Payment. No performance-based release. Fails the fallback and approaches walk-away. Given HDI's reciprocal § 6.3 restriction benefits us, we propose the fallback: cap our restriction at 12 months from the Effective Date with automatic release on HDI's failure to hit the operational date or any service level, delivery date or performance obligation. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2 | Stipulated sum payable by us on any Company termination: (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2, in eight quarterly instalments. Measured against gross Net Sales rather than fees and uncapped — far beyond three months' fees (illustratively ~$600,000 vs ~$140,000 at $2M annual Net Sales) — and triggered even by ordinary § 4.1 non-renewal or termination for HDI's default (only the narrow § 1.6 launch carve-out applies). Proposed deletion; three-month fee cap available as fallback. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 4.1 / § 4.2(a) | Notice mechanics (90 days against a one-year auto-renewing term) sit at the fallback and are not flagged. The material failure is the price of our exit under § 4.2(a), which is uncapped and bites on any Company termination other than § 1.6 launch failure, rendering the convenience right illusory. Proportionate edit: cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees and confirm it is not payable where we terminate for HDI's failure to launch or breach; § 4.2(c) instalment schedule unaffected. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 6.1 (with § 6.2, § 4.1, § 8(b)) | Sits at the fallback and is not redlined: scope limited to defined Deerskin Products plus named competitors; term-only with no post-term tail on us; effectively capped within 12 months via the § 4.1 one-year term and 90-day exit; carve-outs for our closeout website, Joan Cook Catalog products and the grandfathered Globix Agreement. Field of use covers only similar Internet projects, leaving catalog, retail and sourcing unrestricted. Noted, not flagged: "companies similar to" is elastic and there is no acquisitions/internal-development carve-out — to be tightened only if the Agreement is reopened. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 1.4 with § 10.3 | The § 1.4 access/use grant runs to "the Company" alone — no affiliates, no contractors, no notice mechanic — and § 10.3 affirmatively provides that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which excludes them with no path to add them (the rule's walk-away trigger). § 10.3 is otherwise a standard binding-effect clause and does not itself grant an affirmative M&A transfer right. Redline extends § 1.4 to affiliates, contractors acting on our behalf and a successor by merger/acquisition/asset sale, and carves them out of § 10.3; affiliates-on-written-notice offered as fallback. Grant is not stated to be revocable, so no revocability edit needed. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 | Bare successors-and-assigns clause. Positives: no prohibition on Company assignment and no change-of-control trigger anywhere, so HDI cannot exit or re-price on our change of control. But the clause is silent on consent both ways, leaving HDI free to assign this hosting engagement — and our data obligations — to anyone, including a competitor. Redline adds our affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonable-consent gate and no-competitor limit on HDI, leaving the binding language intact. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 | Notice (30 days), business-hours conduct, cost allocation and the narrow scope (payment-calculation records held by our General Manager, no system access) meet or exceed the preferred position.
